defects.title: test_suspended_stock_day_is_nan_on_every_leaf_reader is vacuous for 2 of the 3 readers: both new tradability masks can be deleted and the whole 860-test suite stays green
defects.failure_scenario:
Mutation-verified twice, against the FULL suite, with the mutant instrumented to prove it fired.

(1) Cube reader. Delete `return self._mask_cube(t, tradable)` from engine.py:246 and return the bare tensor (keeping the shape assertion). Result: `tests/ -q` = 860 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed, with the mutant reporting 45 unmasked daily-leaf cube reads actually taken. Yet the behaviour is materially different: on the `daily_view` fixture, `cross_mean(FloatCap, 3)` (a MODE_S round whose only operand IS the daily leaf) changes by max|diff| 1.0e6 over 50 cells.

(2) Panel reader. Make `_run_panel_round.operand`'s branch (engine.py:376-389) return the unmasked (D,S) plane. Result: `tests/ -q` = 860 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed, mutant reporting 21 unmasked panel operands taken. Yet `cs_demean(FloatCap)` changes by max|diff| 1.07e9 over 347 cells and `cs_rank(FloatCap)` by max|diff| 0.2 over 262 cells.

Why the two carriers this test names cannot see it: for `_load_leaf_cube` the carrier is `day_mean(mul(Ret, LimitWidth))`, and `Ret` is already NaN on a suspended stock-day, so `Ret * LimitWidth` is NaN whether or not LimitWidth was masked -- the assertion passes either way. For `_run_panel_round` the carrier is `cs_rank(FloatCap)` and the only assertion is `np.array_equal(np.isnan(p), ~trad.T)`; `_run_panel_round` re-masks every node output unconditionally (engine.py:403-408), so the NaN PATTERN is identical with or without the operand mask -- what the operand mask actually protects is the finite values of the TRADABLE stocks on that day, because cs_* is cross-sectional and an unmasked suspended stock joins the cross-section. Only the `parse("FloatCap")` entry (the `_leaf_panel` path) is non-vacuous; I confirmed that one does go red when its mask is removed.

This is the design's own test-plan bullet ("Masking: a suspended stock-day is NaN in the output on both the cube and the panel path"), so the production code is correct but the guard rail the design asked for does not exist -- and WP8/WP10/WP11 all touch the engine next.
defects.suggested_fix:
Add carriers whose VALUE depends on the leaf's masked value and is not NaN-shadowed by a sibling, and assert values rather than only the NaN pattern.

For `_load_leaf_cube`: `cross_mean(FloatCap, 3)` compared against a hand-written numpy reference built from `np.where(view.tradable(), cap, np.nan)` (a day-axis rolling mean over the masked plane). It is a MODE_S round with the daily leaf as its sole operand, so nothing else can supply the NaN.

For `_run_panel_round.operand`: `cs_demean(FloatCap)` against `cap_masked - nanmean(cap_masked, axis=cross-section)`, i.e. assert the finite values, not just `np.isnan`.

Equivalently (or in addition) add two explicit negative tests that monkeypatch each branch to skip masking and assert `not np.array_equal(...)` -- that makes the claim self-checking rather than relying on a carrier staying well chosen.

defects.title: _leaf_panel is called outside evaluate()'s per-root error handling, so one unresolvable bare DailyFeature root loses the whole tolerant=True batch
defects.failure_scenario:
`evaluate()`'s root loop does `if node.is_leaf: p = self._leaf_panel(node.expr)` with no try/except, while every in-round failure is funnelled into `errors[i]`. Before WP4 that was harmless: the only leaf that survives the `shape.degenerate` root check was a `Constant`, and `np.full` cannot raise. WP4 makes `DailyFeature` degenerate too, so `_leaf_panel` now calls `view.daily(field)`, which raises whenever the field is in `Registry.daily_fields` (so it parses) but not in `view.daily_fields` (so it cannot be resolved) -- exactly the `--daily-root`-not-passed misconfiguration.

Reproduced on the conftest `store` (no daily source attached):
  eng.evaluate([parse("cs_rank(FloatCap)"), parse("cs_rank(day_mean(Close))")], tolerant=True)
    -> errors == {0: "cs_rank: ValueError: dailyfields.resolve: 'FloatCap' needs a daily store carrying it (daily_root)"}, root 1 fine  (correct)
  eng.evaluate([DailyFeature("FloatCap"), parse("cs_rank(day_mean(Close))")], tolerant=True)
    -> raises ValueError out of evaluate(); the healthy second root's panel is lost too  (wrong)

`tolerant=True` is the mode every batch caller uses: gp.py:394, mining/env.py:152 (RL rewarder), mining/boosting.py:168, research.py:119, calculate.py:142, legacy/seed_library.py:35. `is_valid_root` admits a bare `DailyFeature` (expression.py:435), so a seed list, a `calculate.py` factor file or a `research.py --expr FloatCap` is enough -- and WP8 is the package that wires `--daily-root` into exactly those entry points, so it will land on this.

defects.title: _mask_cube's Constant carve-out silently skips the tradability mask for a daily-leaf chunk whose two leading dims are both 1
defects.failure_scenario:
`_mask_cube` short-circuits on `t.shape[0] == 1 and t.shape[1] == 1` (engine.py:231). That guard was written for the `Constant` reader's `torch.full((1, 1, 1), value)`. A daily-leaf chunk is `(hi-lo, D, 1)` in MODE_S and `(S, hi-lo, 1)` in MODE_D, so BOTH leading dims are 1 whenever the chunk is one row and the other axis has length 1 -- and the mask is skipped. A minute `Feature` can never reach that shape, because its last axis is M (24 in the fixture, 241 in production), so the hole arrives with WP4.

Reproduced: a one-day view (`store.view(start=dates[3], end=dates[3])`, where symbol 0 is suspended) with `chunk_symbols=1`:
  CubeEngine(v, chunk_symbols=1)._load_leaf_cube(DailyFeature("LimitWidth"), MODE_S, 0, 1, eng._tradable[0:1, :])
    -> shape (1, 1, 1), value 0.1   (a FINITE value on a stock-day view.tradable() says is suspended)
  the same cell under default chunking -> nan
So the reader itself is not chunk-invariant. The symmetric case is a one-symbol view with `chunk_days=1` in MODE_D, which I also reproduced directly (daily leaf finite on untradable day 3, minute leaf correctly NaN).

I could NOT propagate this to a wrong final panel, and I think it is inert today: the only consumers that spread a leaked cell to other cells are D-axis ops (need D > 1, impossible when MODE_S has shape[1] == D == 1) and S-axis/NT ops (need S > 1, impossible when MODE_D has shape[0] == S == 1); every elementwise / M-axis consumer keeps the leak inside its own stock-day, which the root / panel_out / boundary mask then NaNs. Reported because the reader's contract is broken, the committed shape test cannot see it (it runs with `apply_mask=False`), and the next person to add a width-1 leaf reader or relax `mask_out` inherits a live bug.
defects.suggested_fix:
Don't route the daily leaf through `_mask_cube`'s shape-sniffing carve-out -- the branch already knows the exact shape, because it asserted it two lines earlier. Replace `return self._mask_cube(t, tradable)` at engine.py:246 with:

            if self._mask_needed:
                t = torch.where(tradable.unsqueeze(-1), t,
                                torch.full((), float("nan"), dtype=t.dtype, device=t.device))
            return t

Pin it with a one-day-view / `chunk_symbols=1` test asserting NaN on a suspended stock-day (and the MODE_D mirror).

defects.title: _load_leaf_cube's daily branch hands out a tensor that writes through to view.daily()'s per-view cache
defects.failure_scenario:
In MODE_S, `view.daily_s(field, lo, hi)` returns `self.daily(name)[lo:hi, :]` (store.py:585), which is a C-contiguous VIEW of the array cached in `view._daily[field]`. So `np.ascontiguousarray(sl)` is a no-op, `torch.from_numpy(...)` shares that memory, `.to("cpu", float32)` is a no-op on the default dtype, and when `self._mask_needed` is False `_mask_cube` returns `t` unchanged. The engine then hands kernels a writable tensor aliasing the view's long-lived cache.

Reproduced:
  eng = CubeEngine(view, apply_mask=False)
  t = eng._load_leaf_cube(DailyFeature("FloatCap"), MODE_S, 0, 3, eng._tradable[0:3, :])
  t[0, 0, 0] = -1.0
  view.daily("FloatCap")[0, 0]   # 1000000000.0 -> -1.0
The corruption is not scoped to the chunk or to the call: it persists for the life of the view, across every later expression and every later evaluate().

This is the one reader without the guard the other two have. `_leaf_panel` deliberately uses `astype(..., copy=True)` for exactly this reason (and documents it), and the pre-existing `Feature` path cannot do it because `view.read_s` returns a fresh array on every call (measured: distinct objects, distinct data pointers). Today the only thing standing between this and a silently poisoned view cache is `tests/test_engine.py::test_kernels_never_write_into_operands`. Reachable whenever `_mask_needed` is False: `apply_mask=False`, or any view with no suspended/unlisted stock-days.
defects.suggested_fix: Copy in that branch, matching `_leaf_panel`: replace `np.ascontiguousarray(sl)` at engine.py:245 with `np.array(sl, dtype=self.np_dtype, copy=True)` (or `np.ascontiguousarray(sl).copy()`), and say in the comment that the copy is what detaches the engine from `view._daily`. Cost is one extra copy only on the MODE_S path -- MODE_D's slice is non-contiguous so `ascontiguousarray` already copies, and the masked path already pays it via `torch.where`. Pin it with the three-line write-through test above.

result.notes:
Worktree /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering @ 0d93fa3, `git status` clean before and after (my mutants were pytest plugins loaded from PYTHONPATH outside the tree; scratch work in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP4/). No push, no ssh, nothing outside that scratch dir touched.

WHAT CHECKS OUT (so the coordinator doesn't re-do it)

(a) Design conformance — all 8 implementation steps of "### WP4" and all 5 of "The five engine insertion points" are present and match the design's wording, including the `(hi-lo, n_days)` / `(n_symbols, hi-lo)` shape assertion, the `.unsqueeze(-1)` into (A,B,1), the `(D,S)` transpose, `_daily_t` allocated next to `_bound_advice` and cleared in the existing `finally`, the Constant-before-`values` ordering, `_chunk_sizes` untouched, and the two structural-key branches. No public name or signature added or changed; no `__all__` touched.

(b) Default-path / RNG invariance — holds. Every new code path is `isinstance(..., DailyFeature)`-gated and `DailyFeature` cannot occur in any pre-WP4 tree; `dag.is_leaf`'s widened tuple can only flip False->True for that type. The only unconditional addition is one empty-dict assign + `.clear()` per `evaluate()`. I grepped the whole commit diff for rng/random/seed: the single hit is a docstring reference to `test_chunk_invariance_over_random_population`. The "must not consume an extra `self._rng` draw" constraint genuinely does not apply here (that is WP5/generator.py).

(e) Scope — `git show --stat 0d93fa3` is exactly the 5 owned files, nothing else.

Things I attacked that came out clean: a daily leaf through a real MODE_D round end-to-end (`day_mean(mul(nt_cs_rank(Close), LimitWidth))` plans D[3]) — correct NaN pattern and bit-identical under chunk_days 1/3/7 and chunk_symbols=1; the three readers agree with each other on the same field in one evaluate under 4 chunkings (`cross_delay(FloatCap,0)` vs `mul(FloatCap,1.0)` vs a bare `FloatCap` root — identical); `in_expand(FloatCap)` (the one `restores_m` allowance, since COLLAPSED.collapsed is True) plans S and evaluates; `_align_widths` expands the (A,B,1) leaf with `.contiguous()`, so the stride-0 ULP trap `_materialise` documents is not reachable; `_daily_t`'s field-only key is sound because dtype/device/mask are engine-fixed; `one_layer_keys` (generator.py:53) already treats a spec-less node as a leaf, so the ban machinery does not crash on a daily leaf; `skeleton_key`'s "DF" cannot collide with any other key it emits; clustering's `_hist` skips spec-less nodes. The two cs_* mutants I built (`panel_no_transpose`, `no_daily_cache`) do fail committed tests, so the cache and the transpose ARE pinned — the mask is the specific thing that is not.

Also verified: `test_mask_policies_agree_with_daily_leaves`'s two extra exprs are NOT vacuous (both evaluate with zero errors, so `tolerant=True` is not hiding them).

DEVIATION CLAIMS — both check out, one needs your decision
1. The `cs_rank(Close)` claim is correct and predates WP4: `operand_ok`'s `needs_daily` branch is `return sh.degenerate` with no `strict` parameter (expression.py:189-190), and a bare `Close` is FULL, so `cs_rank(Close)` is unbuildable by any route. The substitution `cs_rank(day_last(Close))` exercises the bullet's intent.
2. Commit attribution is `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5`, not the `Claude Opus 5.5` the computed task asked for. Flagging rather than reporting as a defect: a harness/system attribution instruction does override task text, and the repo's WP2 commit does the same, so the implementer's reasoning is defensible — but the two commits in this branch now carry different co-author lines than the rest, so decide whether you want them normalised.

MINOR, not worth a defect entry
- `self._daily_t` is created only in `evaluate()`, not in `__init__` (unlike `_bound_advice`), so a direct `_run_panel_round` call would AttributeError. No in-repo caller does that, and `_bound_layout` sets the same precedent — but one line in `__init__` would make `_run_panel_round` self-contained.
- `test_load_leaf_cube_shape_assertion_names_both_shapes_on_a_mismatch` asserts only the ACTUAL shape `"(1, 1)"` is in the message, not the expected one, although the design asked for "both shapes named" and the message does name both. Add `"(3, 60)" in msg`.
- `test_daily_t_cache_is_keyed_per_field_name` asserts call counts but never that `cs_rank(FloatCap)` and `cs_rank(LogFloatCap)` give different panels; a wrong key would be caught by the count, but asserting the values too is one line.
- The commit message says "Leaves are never written into `values`" — true for `_run_panel_round`, but `_run_cube_chunk.operand` (engine.py:291-302) does cache leaves in its per-chunk `values`. The code is right; only the blanket phrasing in the message is.
